overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is a municipal regulatory board responsible for adjudicating petitions for dimensional and use variances, special permits, Chapter 40B comprehensive permits, and administrative appeals of building violation notices. Over a span running from March 2024 to September 2026, the board held 26 recorded meetings to evaluate residential alterations, commercial property adjustments, and large-scale multifamily proposals. Major undertakings during this timeframe included the approval of a 289-unit Chapter 40B development at 970 Fellsway and the adjudication of commercial special permits for cannabis establishments. The board also experienced administrative changes, electing board chairs twice and working through backlogged meeting records. As of the September 2026 meeting, the board was focused on evaluating attic expansions and accessory dwelling unit proposals under revised state zoning guidelines while continuing to decide local residential and commercial use requests.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway comprehensive permit
threads.summary: The board conducted an extensive review of an application by The Davis Companies for a 289-unit Chapter 40B multifamily development at 970 Fellsway across several spring 2024 meetings [M02#1, M03#1]. Deliberations involved civil engineering reviews, traffic peer evaluations, stormwater management, and electric vehicle charging provisions [M06#2, M06#3, M06#6]. In May 2024, the board voted that the project's market-rate units were subject to Medford's linkage ordinance [M08#2] and subsequently approved the comprehensive permit with conditions and an off-site improvement fee credit [M09#3]. The board later granted a special permit in January 2025 to demolish part of an adjacent commercial structure to facilitate a lot split preserving required lot coverage for the project [M16#2].

threads.name: 280 Mystic Avenue comprehensive permit
threads.summary: In April 2024, the board scheduled and opened proceedings on a remanded Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application by Combined Properties for a 378-unit residential project at 280 Mystic Avenue [M02#2, M05#1]. The board authorized peer review consultants in architecture, civil engineering, and traffic, and permitted city staff to conduct direct working sessions with the developer [M05#2]. At a May 2024 hearing, the board required the applicant to pay outstanding peer review fees, noted a lack of responsiveness, and continued the hearing [M09#2]. The matter concluded in June 2024 when the board voted to accept the applicant's request to withdraw the comprehensive permit petition [M10#2].

threads.name: Board leadership and administration
threads.summary: The board underwent multiple leadership transitions, electing Jamie Thompson as chair in April 2024 following Mike Caldera's resignation [M04#1], though Caldera continued as acting chair specifically for the 970 Fellsway proceedings [M06#1]. Following Thompson's resignation in early 2025 [M17#3], the board re-elected Mike Caldera as chair in February 2025 [M18#1]. In addition to tracking vacant board seats and appointments from the Mayor's office [M18#7, M21#2], members addressed administrative operations by forming a subcommittee to overhaul outdated rules and regulations [M11#3, M13#2]. The board also dealt with an ongoing backlog of meeting minutes by testing transcription and AI software tools [M09#9, M17#3, M18#7].

threads.name: Accessory dwelling units and state regulations
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board approved setback variances for an attached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on Fulton Street [M24#6] while continuing two companion attic-expansion ADU applications on Vassar Street and Wellesley Street to consult legal counsel regarding new state zoning regulations [M24#3, M24#4]. The Vassar and Wellesley Street petitions were continued again in August 2026 to ensure voting consistency among members [M25#1]. In September 2026, the board postponed both petitions to October 2026 to allow the applicant to submit modified, smaller designs and to obtain further legal guidance on state ADU guidelines [M26#1, M26#2].

threads.name: Automotive business variances and transitions
threads.summary: The board addressed multiple cases involving automotive facilities seeking zoning relief or site conversions. In April 2024, after seeking legal counsel on notice discrepancies [M01#3], the board granted a use variance allowing Class 2 motor vehicle sales at an existing repair shop at 38 Harvard Avenue [M04#4], subsequently granting a six-month extension in June 2025 [M19#2]. In May 2024, the board approved an amended height variance to allow the construction of a three-story auto dealership facility and car elevator at 400 Mystic Avenue [M09#7]. Later, the board reviewed and approved use and dimensional variances allowing the demolition of a nonconforming motor vehicle repair station at 85 Elm Street to build a three-unit residential townhouse [M16#1, M18#3].

threads.name: Cannabis dispensary special permits at 114 Mystic Avenue
threads.summary: In May 2026, the board heard applications by Victory Gardens for commercial cannabis operations at 114 Mystic Avenue, granting special permits for medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing [M22#2]. The associated request to authorize courier delivery services was continued to seek input from the police chief [M22#2] and was continued again in June 2026 while awaiting legal counsel [M23#1]. The review concluded in July 2026 when the board approved the special permit allowing cannabis delivery services from the site [M24#1].

threads.name: Residential conversions and multi-unit relief
threads.summary: The board consistently adjudicated requests to expand residential density or convert single-family properties into multi-family dwellings. While it denied a special permit and variances to convert a detached garage into a fourth residential unit at 52 Garfield Avenue due to a lack of hardship [M04#8], it approved lot width variances to convert a single-family house to a two-family dwelling at 13 Marion Street [M12#3] and permitted the creation of an undersized lot at 7 Grant Avenue [M16#3]. The board also reviewed proposals to replace single-family homes with two-family structures, approving relief at 121 Second Street after design revisions addressed scale and massing [M20#1, M21#1]. In 2026, the board approved conversions from single-family to two-family dwellings on Main Street [M23#7] and Surrey Street [M25#2], and granted a use variance to construct a second single-family home on Sturgis Street [M26#3].

periods.narrative: The board handled major Chapter 40B comprehensive permit reviews for large multifamily developments at 970 Fellsway and 280 Mystic Avenue while navigating internal chair elections. Members also adjudicated regular dockets of residential dimensional variances, multi-family conversions, and procedural updates to board regulations.

The board reviewed commercial special permits, including adult-use cannabis operations on Mystic Avenue, and resolved residential variance applications and administrative violation appeals. Deliberations during this term increasingly focused on applying and seeking legal interpretation for state regulations governing accessory dwelling units.
